h1: SC Park Hotel Bangkok — the large full-service 4-star in Wang Thonglang, with pool, three restaurants and free parking near Vejthani Hospital
intro: When a family member needs treatment at Vejthani Hospital, or you simply need a well-equipped base on Bangkok's east side, SC Park Hotel Bangkok offers something rare in this part of the city: a genuine full-service property with a pool, multiple dining venues and ample free parking, all in one place · the hotel sits at Soi Ramkhamhaeng 39, Wang Thonglang, on a spacious plot that has been open since 1996 · 210 rooms ranging from Superior to Luxury Suite · Vejthani Hospital (JCI-accredited, 263 beds, at 1 Soi Lat Phrao 111, Bang Kapi) is approximately 5.5 km away — about a 12-minute drive in normal traffic via Grab or private car · rates start from approx. THB 1,300/night · the hotel scores 8.8 out of 10 from 605 reviews on Trip.com · this review is compiled from real guest feedback across Booking.com, Agoda and TripAdvisor — we have not stayed here ourselves.

body.html: Who SC Park Hotel suits best — this property serves two audiences particularly well. The first is families or companions accompanying a patient at Vejthani Hospital, who need more than a bare-bones guesthouse for a multi-day stay: a pool to unwind in, somewhere to eat three meals without going out, and free parking for a car they drive to the hospital every day. The second is corporate groups and events organisers looking for a conference venue in the Ramkhamhaeng–Lat Phrao corridor, since the hotel holds TCEP-certified meeting rooms that seat anywhere from 15 to 350 people, along with a ballroom for weddings and banquets. What makes the combination unusual is having all of this — pool, squash court, gym, three restaurants and a large car park — under one roof at a price that sits well below Bangkok's five-star tier. If you need a full-service base on the east side of the city without the noise and cost of Sukhumvit, SC Park Hotel fills that gap effectively.

Location and getting around — the hotel is at 474 Soi Ramkhamhaeng 39 (Thepleela 1), Phlabphla, Wang Thonglang, Bangkok 10310, set in a quieter residential district well away from the tourist buzz of central Bangkok. For Vejthani Hospital visits, the hospital's address is 1 Soi Lat Phrao 111, Khlong Chan, Bang Kapi — about 5.5 km by road, roughly 12–15 minutes by car or Grab in normal conditions (allow extra time during the morning and evening rush hours). The route runs via Ramkhamhaeng Road and connects to Lat Phrao via Pradit Manutham Road, which is straightforward. The nearest rail station is MRT Yellow Line Hua Mak, approximately 2 km away — a five-to-seven-minute Grab ride rather than a walk. It needs to be said plainly: the hotel is not within walking distance of any rail station, and the east-Bangkok location means central shopping and nightlife areas require a 30-minute-plus journey. For guests who have their own car or are content to use Grab, this is not a problem; for independent sightseers who plan to live on the BTS, it is a genuine limitation worth considering before booking.
"Room was spotless, breakfast had an enormous spread — easily the best hotel breakfast I've had in this price range. Kids loved the pool. Staff sorted every request before I even had to ask twice."

Room types and what guests actually find — the 210 rooms cover a wide span: Superior, Deluxe, Super Deluxe, Junior Suite, Executive Suite, Executive Suite Plus, Connecting Room and Luxury Suite. The Connecting Room option is particularly valued by families travelling with a patient, as two adjoining rooms provide privacy for both caregiver and patient. Real reviews consistently describe rooms as spacious for the price, with many noting that the square footage surprised them given the nightly rate. The decoration is Thai-contemporary — warm, comfortable, not cutting-edge but functional. That said, the hotel opened in 1996 and the age of the building shows unevenly across the property: some reviewers praised genuinely well-maintained rooms, while others reported mouldy air-conditioning units, a musty smell in certain rooms, and occasional bathroom flooding. The gap between the best and worst rooms at SC Park is noticeably wider than at a recently built property. The honest approach is to request a recently renovated unit at check-in — and to ask for a room change immediately if the one you're given falls short.

Facilities: the real draw — this is what separates SC Park from most competitors in the same price band on Bangkok's east side. The outdoor pool has a distinctive curved shape and is landscaped with mature trees; it sits alongside a children's pool, making it genuinely family-friendly. Multiple reviews specifically praise the pool water quality as consistently clean and clear. Beyond the pool: a gym, a squash court (a rarity at this price point), a sauna, and a free car park large enough to accommodate the hotel's full guest load — something practically impossible to find at comparable hotels in central Bangkok. On the dining side, AT22 Restaurant serves Thai and international food including an acclaimed breakfast buffet, East Ocean offers Chinese cuisine that earns its own positive reviews, and Coffee'n Cream handles coffee, pastries and lighter meals throughout the day. The MARBLE BAR and BICARO round out the evening options. Guests who don't want to leave the compound for three meals a day can comfortably avoid doing so — which matters when your daily routine revolves around hospital visits.

What real reviews actually say — the honest version — across Booking.com, Agoda, TripAdvisor and Trip.com, the pattern is consistent and worth spelling out clearly. On the positive side: the breakfast buffet draws glowing comments from a large proportion of guests, describing it as one of the best value hotel breakfasts in Bangkok; the pool is repeatedly praised for cleanliness; staff receive strong marks for friendliness and problem-solving; the room sizes and free parking generate genuine satisfaction. On the problematic side: several reviewers report dirty or mouldy air-conditioning units (one guest used the specific phrase "very dirty AC" with supporting details); Wi-Fi is flagged as unreliable in multiple reviews, with guests saying they resorted to mobile data; bathroom flooding appears in a handful of reports; and mattress firmness draws complaints from guests who find the beds harder than expected. None of these are dealbreakers for guests who catch a good room — but the inconsistency means it is worth stating expectations plainly and being prepared to request a change if needed.

"Air conditioning was very dirty and the WiFi barely works — ended up using my phone data the whole stay. That said, the pool and breakfast were both genuinely good, and the free parking made life easy with the car."

SC Park for Vejthani Hospital visitors specifically — Vejthani Hospital is a JCI-accredited tertiary care facility with 263 beds that treats over 300,000 patients annually including a large proportion of international medical tourists. It specialises in orthopaedic surgery, oncology and multi-specialty care, meaning many patients and their families face stays of several days or weeks. For that context, the practical calculation at SC Park Hotel runs like this: the hotel is 5.5 km by road, approximately 12–15 minutes by Grab in normal traffic (Grab is inexpensive and plentiful in Bangkok, and the hospital's drop-off point is straightforward from this direction). In exchange for that short commute, you gain a full-service hotel with a pool to decompress in after long hospital days, enough dining variety that no one needs to arrange food separately each meal, and free parking if a relative is driving in from the suburbs. Hotels within walking distance of Vejthani tend to be smaller guesthouses without these facilities. Whether the trade-off suits you depends on whether the additional comfort of a full-service property justifies a 12-minute drive — for extended stays, many families find it does.

Price and value — standard Superior rooms start from roughly THB 1,300–1,500/night in the shoulder period, rising to around THB 2,000–2,700 for Junior Suites and Executive rooms in peak season or around public holidays (equivalent to approximately USD 35–76 at current exchange rates). Against the full-service offering — pool, gym, squash, sauna, three restaurants, free parking, meeting facilities — the rate sits at a fair point for Bangkok's 4-star segment. The caveat is the location discount built into those prices: you are paying less partly because the east-Bangkok address is less convenient than Sukhumvit or Siam. For a medical-tourism stay or a corporate trip to the area, that location discount works in your favour. For leisure travel that requires constant movement across the city, a centrally located hotel would likely serve better despite the higher tariff.

highlights.title: Pool, children's pool, squash court and sauna
highlights.text: A curved outdoor pool set among mature trees, a separate children's pool, plus gym, squash court and sauna — unusually complete facilities at this price point in east Bangkok.

highlights.title: Three restaurants and a praised breakfast buffet
highlights.text: AT22 (Thai/international), East Ocean (Chinese) and Coffee'n Cream open daily. The breakfast buffet draws the hotel's most consistent five-star comments across all review platforms.

highlights.title: Free parking · ~12-min drive to Vejthani Hospital
highlights.text: A large free car park — rare in Bangkok — makes daily drives to Vejthani Hospital (5.5 km) straightforward. Essential for families managing a long-term medical stay.

honestSummary: SC Park Hotel Bangkok is a full-service 4-star property that delivers a pool, squash court, three restaurants and free parking in one compound at a price that makes sense for east Bangkok · it works particularly well for families managing a multi-day stay near Vejthani Hospital (~5.5 km, ~12-min drive), and for corporate groups needing conference space in the Ramkhamhaeng corridor · the honest caveats are real: room quality is inconsistent — some units have mouldy AC and weak Wi-Fi — and the location is remote from any rail station · ask for a recently renovated room at check-in, and bring mobile data as a backup.
honestChecks: If consistent room quality matters to you — rooms vary noticeably across this ageing building; some units have dirty AC units, musty odours or bathroom flooding → ask for a recently renovated room at check-in and request an immediate change if yours has problems; always book with free cancellation

If you rely on hotel Wi-Fi for work or communication — multiple reviews describe the signal as barely functional in the rooms → bring a local SIM card or use your phone as a hotspot; do not count on the hotel's Wi-Fi for anything time-sensitive

If you want to sightsee central Bangkok by public transport — the nearest MRT station (Yellow Line Hua Mak) is roughly 2 km away with no direct walking route → this hotel suits guests with a car or those happy to use Grab; for leisure travel centred on Sukhumvit or Siam, a more central property will save significant daily travel time

tips.title: Use Grab for Vejthani Hospital — it is simple
tips.body: Vejthani Hospital is 5.5 km away — a 12-to-15-minute Grab ride in normal traffic. Grab is cheap, plentiful and picks up from the hotel entrance. More practical than working out bus routes.

tips.title: Hit the pool before 8 am
tips.body: The pool is quietest in the early morning — ideal for lap swimming or a calm soak before hospital visits. It fills up with families and children from mid-morning onwards.

tips.title: Ask for a recently renovated room
tips.body: The building opened in 1996 and room quality varies. Request a higher floor or a unit that has recently been refurbished. If your room has dirty AC, a musty smell or plumbing issues, the front desk will change it — just ask.

tips.title: Bring a local SIM or mobile hotspot
tips.body: Hotel Wi-Fi is flagged as weak in multiple guest reviews. If your work or medical coordination depends on a reliable internet connection, do not count on the hotel network — have a local data SIM as a backup.

faqTitle: SC Park Hotel Bangkok — Frequently Asked Questions

faq.q: Where is SC Park Hotel Bangkok located, and is it near public transport?
faq.a: The hotel is at 474 Soi Ramkhamhaeng 39 (Thepleela 1), Phlabphla, Wang Thonglang, Bangkok 10310. The nearest rail station is MRT Yellow Line Hua Mak, approximately 2 km away — a five-to-seven-minute Grab ride. The hotel is not within walking distance of any train station. It suits guests who have a car or are comfortable using Grab; for heavy public-transport users it is less convenient.

faq.q: How far is SC Park Hotel from Vejthani Hospital?
faq.a: Vejthani Hospital (1 Soi Lat Phrao 111, Bang Kapi, JCI-accredited) is approximately 5.5 km by road — about 12–15 minutes by Grab or private car under normal traffic conditions. Allow extra time during Bangkok rush hours (07:00–09:00 and 17:00–20:00). The route runs via Ramkhamhaeng Road and Pradit Manutham Road. SC Park is a good base for multi-day medical stays due to its full-service amenities.

faq.q: Does SC Park Hotel Bangkok have a swimming pool and free parking?
faq.a: Yes to both. The outdoor pool has a distinctive curved shape landscaped with mature trees, plus a separate children's pool. The pool water quality is consistently praised across multiple review platforms. Free parking is a significant advantage — large, well-organised and genuinely rare at this price point in Bangkok.

faq.q: What is the breakfast like at SC Park Hotel Bangkok?
faq.a: The international breakfast buffet at AT22 Restaurant is consistently the most praised aspect of SC Park Hotel across all review platforms. Guests describe a wide selection of both Asian and Western dishes, good quality and generous portions. It is included in some room packages — check when booking. Beyond breakfast, East Ocean (Chinese restaurant) and Coffee'n Cream (café and bakery) are both open daily.

faq.q: Are there any known problems with rooms at SC Park Hotel Bangkok?
faq.a: To be honest about what real guests report: some rooms have dirty or mouldy air-conditioning units, and Wi-Fi is weak or unreliable in parts of the building. A smaller number of reviews mention bathroom flooding or hard mattresses. Room quality is uneven across this 1996-built property. The good news is that many guests have clean, well-maintained rooms — the recommendation is to ask for a recently renovated room at check-in, request an immediate swap if yours has issues, and bring a local SIM card for reliable internet access.
